hero.subtitle: When someone else's carelessness takes a family member in Woodside, California law gives certain survivors a way to seek accountability. LawProactive quietly connects you with an independent wrongful death attorney, at no cost to you.

about.title: Woodside Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Woodside is a small place. With about 5,561 residents spread across the wooded hills of San Mateo County, a death here is rarely anonymous — neighbors notice, and the loss ripples through the whole community. Public records show 42 injury collisions on Woodside's roads in 2025, with 57 people hurt and no traffic deaths recorded that year. Even so, families in town still lose loved ones to serious crashes on Rt 84, Woodside Road, Portola Road and La Honda Road, to workplace incidents, to medical errors, and to hazards on someone else's property. When a death traces back to another person's carelessness, California law gives the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children the first right to bring a civil wrongful death claim. Other dependents and heirs may qualify as well. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that listens to what happened and connects your family with an independent attorney who handles wrongful death cases and works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Woodside Families Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to the spouse or domestic partner and children first, with certain dependents and heirs eligible in some circumstances. An attorney can sort out your family's position before anyone files.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the window is shorter when a government entity is involved. A connected attorney can flag which timeline applies to your situation right away.

items.title: A full picture of your losses
items.desc: Recoverable losses reach beyond funeral and burial costs to include lost financial support and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance. An independent lawyer can help make sure nothing is overlooked.

items.question: Public records show no traffic deaths in Woodside for 2025. Does that mean a wrongful death claim isn't realistic here?
items.answer: Not at all. Wrongful death claims arise from many causes beyond crashes, including medical negligence, workplace incidents, and dangerous conditions on property. Woodside residents are also injured or killed while traveling outside town limits, and a claim follows the facts, not the city line. If a loved one died because of someone else's carelessness, it is worth a conversation.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we still need a civil case?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate. A criminal case is brought by the state to punish wrongdoing, while a wrongful death claim is a civil action your family brings to recover your own losses. One can proceed regardless of what happens in the other, and the standards of proof differ.

items.question: What if the crash happened on Rt 84 or another state-maintained road and we think the roadway was a factor?
items.answer: Claims that involve a government entity, such as the state agency responsible for a highway, follow a much shorter deadline than the usual two years. Missing that window can end the claim before it starts. This is one reason families are encouraged to speak with an attorney soon after a loss rather than waiting.
